messages.subject: DIVALIKE models halted by: "Note: tipranges_to_tip_condlikes_of_data_on_each_state()"
parts:
Dear all,

I am currently running DEC/BAYARELIKE/DIVALIKE + t + m as well as their + j versions in the case of a trinary trait.

I could run all models successfully on my Mac laptop (R v4.0.2, BioGeoBEARS v1.1.2).

I then tried on our HPC cluster (R v3.6.1, BioGeoBEARS v1.1.2) and all models could run using the exact same scripts, except for the two DIVALIKE models for which I get the error below.

Thanks a lot in advance for your insights.

Best,

Simon

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

> BioGeoBEARS_run_object = fix_BioGeoBEARS_params_minmax(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

> check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

Read 7 items

Read 552 items

[1] TRUE

>

> # For a slow analysis, run once, then set runslow=FALSE to just

> # load the saved result.

> runslow = TRUE

> resfn = "combined_DIVALIKE.Rdata"

> if (runslow)

+ {

+   res = bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object, skip_optim=FALSE)

+

+   save(res, file=resfn)

+   resDIVALIKE_combined = res

+ } else {

+   # Loads to "res"

+   load(resfn)

+   resDIVALIKE_combined = res

+ }

Note: tipranges_to_tip_condlikes_of_data_on_each_state() is

      creating 'states_list' automatically.

[1] "Note: tipranges_to_tip_condlikes_of_data_on_each_state() is converting a states_list with (0-based) numbers to the equivalent areanames"

Execution : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

Execution stopped

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] DIVALIKE models halted by: "Note: tipranges_to_tip_condlikes_of_data_on_each_state()"
parts: Hi -- if it works on one computer but not another, and one model but not another, it is going to be pretty challenging to figure out what is happening.  The "Note: tipranges..." part is irrelevant, this is the issue:
"Execution : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors"

...but why that would occur on one machine and not another one is mystifying.  It maybe suggests you might have a state space of 1 state/range somewhere, but even that should work if it works anywhere.

Please do make sure there are no source() commands left in the script you are running (this could load old code, although probably not).

Your best bet: restrict the minimums of free parameters, e.g. change the minimums from 0.000000001 to 0.001, this might avoid an underflow problem if that is the issue.

Cheers,
Nick

Dear Nick,

Thanks a lot for your reply. I indeed misread the error.

I "somehow" managed to make that last model to run on the cluster after a lot of trials (including changing the minimums of free parameters).

No attempt was fruitful in the previous sessions, but today it was. I have no idea why that is, except that I was most likely working on a different node than last time. This mysterious behaviour was maybe caused by a faulty node?

All the best,
Simon
